newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS-Czech c.bank rate hike seen steadying crown.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Czech c.bank rate hike seen steadying crown.

text.p: The Czech central bank's hike in its Lombard last-resort lending rate to 50 percent from 14 percent on Friday should give some badly-needed stability for the sagging crown, analysts said.

Czech National Bank (CNB) board member Ludek Niedermeyer told Reuters that the move was part of a three-pronged strategy in response to short-selling which had pushed the crown to record lows in recent days.
After two days of failing to boost the crown through direct market intervention, the move should be enough to ensure some stability in the coming days, analysts said.

"It was quite a logical step. It looks like the intervention was not helping too much...so the only way to change the crown's direction was on the interest rate side," said Tomas Novak of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka (CSOB)
"It looks as though the central bank is prepared to move even more on the interest rate side, so I guess the crown will stabilise somewhat," he added.
The crown has been under heavy pressure over the past week on selling mainly from foreign investors.

It hit a record weak point of five percent below parity in the dollar/mark basket which the central bank uses to fix its value daily. This prompted the CNB to intervene on the market for the first time in over a year.
But the interventions over two days failed to scare off bears who continued to push the crown lower and analysts said stronger action was needed if the crown were to claw its way back toward parity.
"Some of the bigger players smell blood, they know the central bank right now is weak and there is a chance to push the crown out of the band and they just might," said one trader.

Niedermeyer said that in addition to raising the Lombard rate, the CNB would also "restrict the access of the banks to the Lombard window if necessary and we will adequately change the repo rate in our future open market operations".
"Normally the Lombard rate is not used, but because banks are spending domestic currency and buying foreign currency, there could be a liquidity shortage," he said.
"In such a circumstance, the central bank is not very happy to provide financing of speculation against the domestic currency," he added.
The Lombard rate is a last-resort lending facility for banks.

Niedermeyer said the third stage of the strategy could involve a further raising of the repo rate -- which was hiked 50 basis points to 12.9 percent earlier on Friday -- depending on market conditions.

"It will depend on the concrete situation on the money market and forex market on Monday morning," he said. "We expect that after some wave of short-selling is over, then we will not need extremely high interest rates, but we are ready to use them if the market is volatile."
The crown firmed immediately after Niedermeyer's statement and rose to about 2.6 percent below its parity rate in late trading from 4.19 percent below before he spoke.

But Ota Otepka of ING bank warned that while the central bank's actions would firm up the crown, the economy could pay a heavy price in return. "Of course they can hold the Czech crown where it is, but it may kill the economy in the process," he said.

The economy is already showing signs of a sharp slowdown with Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus predicting first quarter GDP growth would be zero. It would be a success if full year growth hit 2.7 percent, half of the government's original estimate, he said.
